submission:
Root cause: At 06:52:47-06:52:48 the platform-automation pipeline moved every hotel-reservation mongod container from mongo:4.4.6 to mongo:8.0.14-rc0, a multi-major jump onto a pre-release build, as the last change before onset [tr_73ec19bd8628][tr_2cae39058274][tr_baad9dab95a5]. The new binary cannot complete startup: each mongod logs an orderly, self-initiated shutdown from the initandlisten thread with exit code 62 (mongod's version/on-disk-format incompatibility abort) at 06:53:47 (rate), 06:53:49 (geo) and 06:53:53 (user) [tr_56d7f7ea455d][tr_b6ac44351d92][tr_bcb3a8416cae]. The processes never reach a listening state, so all five mongodb services alert together at 06:53:54 as their pods crash-loop. The running artifact is not one that can start here; the fix is to restore the 4.4.6 image.
Faulty component: mongodb-geo
Fault type: bad_deploy
Confidence: high

Evidence:
- The entire mongodb-geo workload was stood up fresh inside the window: workload first creation, Service, PVC, and the mongo-geo-script ConfigMap all landed between 06:51:58 and 06:52:00, roughly a minute before onset. (found, from change_history on mongodb-geo)
- The container image was moved from a long-standing 4.4.6 release to an 8.0.14-rc0 release-candidate tag at 06:52:47 — a multi-major-version jump onto a pre-release build, and the last change before onset. (found, from change_history on mongodb-geo)
- A new ConfigMap named failure-admin-geo was created at 06:52:01 and, at 06:52:04, a corresponding volume plus a volumeMount at /scripts was added to the mongo container; the pre-existing mounts (/data/db, /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d) were left intact. The naming is consistent with deliberate fault-injection material being mounted into the database container. (found, from change_history on mongodb-geo)
- The geo-pvc PersistentVolumeClaim was created at 06:52:00 and then modified twice at 06:52:08, so storage binding for this instance was still settling seconds before the image change. (found, from change_history on mongodb-geo)
- All ten changes were attributed to the same actor, platform-automation, and all fall within a 49-second burst; there is no second, independent change stream. (found, from change_history on mongodb-geo)
- The failure is gradual drift or latent decay in a long-running instance, so the trigger lies outside the change record. (ruled_out, from change_history on mongodb-geo; why: The workload itself was first created inside the window; there is no long-running instance to have drifted. Every artifact backing this service is under a minute older than onset.)
- An operator made a manual, out-of-band edit that bypassed the deployment pipeline. (ruled_out, from change_history on mongodb-geo; why: All ten recorded changes carry the same automation actor; no human-attributed or ad-hoc change appears in the window.)
- The incident was caused by a resource-limit change — CPU/memory requests or limits tightened, triggering throttling or OOM. (ruled_out, from change_history on mongodb-geo; why: The change set contains image, volume, volumeMount, PVC, Service and ConfigMap operations only; no resource-spec change is recorded.)
- A scaling or replica-count change (scale-to-zero, scale-down, rollout surge) caused the loss of capacity. (ruled_out, from change_history on mongodb-geo; why: No replica or scaling operation appears among the ten changes; the only workload-level events are initial creation and the image update.)
- The existing init-script mount or mongo-geo-script ConfigMap contents were altered, breaking database initialisation. (ruled_out, from change_history on mongodb-geo; why: The mongo-geo-script ConfigMap was created and never subsequently modified, and the diff shows the /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d mount carried through unchanged; the only mount delta is the added /scripts entry.)
- Storage was never provisioned — the PVC is absent and the pod cannot bind a volume. (ruled_out, from change_history on mongodb-geo; why: geo-pvc was explicitly created at 06:52:00 and updated twice thereafter, so the claim object exists; absence of a PVC is not the explanation.)
- The image change was a routine patch-level bump unlikely to alter behaviour. (ruled_out, from change_history on mongodb-geo; why: The recorded transition crosses several major versions and lands on a release-candidate tag, which is not a patch-level move.)
- mongodb-user received 7 changes, all attributed to the platform-automation actor, clustered within roughly two minutes immediately preceding the onset timestamp (06:52:01-06:52:48 versus onset ~06:53:54). (found, from change_history on mongodb-user)
- The highest-suspicion change is a container image update for the user mongo workload, moving from a 4.4.x stable tag to an 8.0.x release-candidate tag — a multi-major-version jump onto a pre-release build, applied about one minute before onset. (found, from change_history on mongodb-user)
- The change set describes a fresh stand-up rather than an in-place tweak: the workload container, the Service object, and the PersistentVolumeClaim were all created in this window, with the PVC then modified four more times before the image update landed. Reasoning:
Three independent change queries show the same act on three different instances: same actor, same ~47-second burst, same 4.4.6 -> 8.0.14-rc0 image move last in sequence [tr_73ec19bd8628][tr_2cae39058274][tr_baad9dab95a5]. That explains five simultaneous alerts from a seed the graph does not connect - they share a rollout, not a call path. Three independent log queries show the same symptom: exit code 62 in the initandlisten context with a complete sub-20ms shutdownTask and a clean WiredTiger close [tr_56d7f7ea455d][tr_b6ac44351d92][tr_bcb3a8416cae]. The process exits under its own control before accepting any client, which closes OOM/SIGKILL, load saturation, hangs and graceful orchestrator stops; the clean storage-engine close and successful fs-lock removal argue against an unreadable or full store. What remains is a binary that refuses to run against what it finds. Both metrics dispatches failed structurally - these services emit no span-derived metrics [tr_d1c94edb180d][tr_af3c6cb81e1c] - so no resource curve was available either way.

Alternatives considered:
1. mongodb-geo: The mongodb volumes hold content the binary cannot decode on read, aborting startup. (datastore_corruption). Ranked lower because: WiredTiger opened and closed cleanly on all three instances with successful rollback-to-stable and checkpoint and no storage errors [tr_b6ac44351d92][tr_bcb3a8416cae][tr_56d7f7ea455d]; the abort appeared only after the image moved, pointing at the artifact rather than the contents.
2. mongodb-geo: The failure-admin-geo ConfigMap mounted at /scripts supplies a startup directive that makes mongod abort. (bad_config). Ranked lower because: That mount is reported only for mongodb-geo [tr_73ec19bd8628], yet rate and user show the identical exit-62 startup abort [tr_56d7f7ea455d][tr_bcb3a8416cae]; the only change common to all three is the image.

Open questions:
- The triggering assertion line before each shutdown was never retrieved; all three log results are truncated to the shutdown tail [tr_b6ac44351d92][tr_bcb3a8416cae][tr_56d7f7ea455d], so exit 62's meaning rests on convention, not this environment's own error text.
- Why freshly created PVCs would carry data the 8.0 binary rejects - recommendation-pvc was created at 06:52:00 inside the same burst [tr_baad9dab95a5], explicitly ruling out a reused 4.4-era volume there.
- mongodb-profile was never dispatched against; its participation is inferred from the other four, and the failure-admin-geo ConfigMap mounted at /scripts on geo only [tr_73ec19bd8628] was never read.
